answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. The canyon decay curve is applied at each close, cedar records the drop, and dawn recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 6 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 168 aliases cost 347 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
